titleEn: Stay Where You Can See the Green Vest!

pages.text: "Grandpa, there are lots of pinecones here!" Nils the little bear called, pushing aside fallen leaves. The autumn woods were all brown. Only Grandpa's knitted vest was green.
"I will fill my basket!" Nils picked up pinecones one by one. Behind him, Grandpa Bruno bundled branches. "Stay where you can see my vest. If you cannot see it, stop right where you are."
There were more pinecones over there. Nils went that way. Farther on, there were even more. He went that way too. Rustle, rustle. His basket grew heavier.
When the basket was half full, Nils looked up. Brown trees, brown trees, more brown trees. The green vest was nowhere in sight. His heart thumped fast.

Nils was about to run, but stopped. He remembered the promise Grandpa had made while pointing to his vest: if it disappears, stop right there. Phew—one deep breath. "I will not run. I will call from here."
Nils put down his basket and called loudly. "Grandpa—!" Only leaves rustled. He called again. "Grandpa—!" Far away, a rustling sound came closer.
A green dot appeared between the brown trees. Grandpa's vest! Nils jumped. "Stay where you can see the green vest! Now I understand!"
Grandpa strode up and wrapped his broad palm around Nils's paw. "You stayed and called instead of running. Well done." The racing heart slowed to a gentle thump, thump.

Picking up pinecones again, Nils recited three rules. "One, stay where you can see the vest! Two, if it disappears, stop! Three, call loudly!" Even while picking, he glanced at the green dot. "Stay where you can see the green vest!"

The basket was full. Nils buried his face in the green vest. Grandpa stroked his back. Even farther away, Nils was not scared when he could see the vest. He raised both paws above his head. "Stay where you can see the green vest!"
